name: Easter Island (Rapa Nui), Chile
clues: I am a crowd that never speaks, nearly a thousand heads with no bodies to walk, and most of us turn our backs to the waves.
Riddle me this: the most remote people on Earth carved giants, then raced each spring to fetch a single bird's egg.
Giant carved heads called moai. Part of Chile, deep in the Pacific.
fact: Most moai face inland, watching over the villages that carved them.

name: Hermitage Museum, St Petersburg, Russia
clues: I hold three million treasures, yet my most famous guards are furry, whiskered, and paid in fish.
Once an emperor's winter home, now my halls of green and white would take you years to walk through.
A giant art museum on the Neva River.
fact: The Hermitage was founded by Catherine the Great in 1764.

name: Taipei 101, Taiwan
clues: I have a heart of steel the size of a house, and it swings so I don't when the storms come.
I'm stacked like eight bamboo stalks, and I count my floors with a number you'd use to start a class.
A skyscraper in Taiwan's capital.
fact: Taipei 101 was the tallest building in the world from 2004 to 2010.

name: Plitvice Lakes, Croatia
clues: Water is my staircase: sixteen steps of blue and green, each one spilling into the next.
My colors change with the minerals and the light, and only wooden boardwalks let you walk on my water.
A national park of terraced lakes in Croatia.
fact: The lakes are separated by natural dams of travertine that are still growing.

name: Okavango Delta, Botswana
clues: I am a river that never reaches the sea: I die of thirst in the desert and give life as I go.
Every winter, rain that fell far away arrives late, and my sand turns to a swamp full of elephants.
A giant inland delta in Botswana.
fact: The Okavango floods at the height of the dry season, because the rain falls months earlier in Angola.

name: Matterhorn, Switzerland and Italy
clues: I am a crooked tooth of stone on the border of two nations, and a famous chocolate wears my face.
I'm a pyramid no pharaoh built, and the first men to reach my top paid for it on the way down.
A pyramid-shaped peak above Zermatt.
fact: The Matterhorn was first climbed in 1865 by Edward Whymper's team.

name: Meteora, Greece
clues: Monks once climbed up my stone pillars in nets and baskets, as if heaven had a doorstep.
My name means 'suspended in the air', and I am a handful of monasteries perched on rock towers.
Monasteries on top of rock pillars in central Greece.
fact: Six of Meteora's monasteries are still active today.

name: Chichen Itza, Mexico
clues: Clap at my foot and I chirp back like a sacred bird; I am a calendar made of stone steps.
Twice a year, the sunset sends a feathered serpent of shadow sliding down my staircase.
The great Maya pyramid of El Castillo in the Yucatán.
fact: El Castillo has 91 steps on each of its four sides, plus the top platform, for 365 in all.

name: Golden Gate Bridge, San Francisco, USA
clues: I am painted the color of a sunset, though my builders only meant to stop the rust.
Fog swallows me most mornings, yet I'm the most photographed way to cross a famous strait.
A red-orange suspension bridge across a Californian strait.
fact: When it opened in 1937, the Golden Gate had the longest main span of any suspension bridge in the world.

name: Charles Bridge, Prague, Czechia
clues: Thirty saints stand guard on my back, and touching one of them is said to bring you back again.
I'm a stone path over a river where kings once walked to be crowned and kings' enemies' heads were hung.
A medieval stone bridge over the Vltava River.
fact: Construction of Charles Bridge began in 1357.

name: Cliffs of Moher, Ireland
clues: I am a wall the ocean has been punching for millions of years, and I'm still 200 metres tall.
Puffins nest on my face, and wizards and pirates have both been filmed on my edge.
Famous sea cliffs in County Clare, Ireland.
fact: The Cliffs of Moher stretch for about 14 km.

name: Giant's Causeway, Northern Ireland
clues: A giant built me as stepping stones to a rival across the sea, or so the story goes.
I'm made of forty thousand stone columns, mostly six-sided, as if a honeycomb turned to rock.
Basalt columns on the coast of County Antrim.
fact: The columns formed about 60 million years ago when lava cooled and cracked.

name: Baikonur Cosmodrome, Kazakhstan
clues: The first man to leave the Earth started his trip from my steppe, and I'm still where many rides to the sky begin.
I'm a launch pad in the middle of the desert, rented by one country from another.
The world's first and largest spaceport, on the Kazakh steppe.
fact: Yuri Gagarin launched from Baikonur on 12 April 1961.

name: Machu Picchu, Peru
clues: Hidden in the clouds, I was forgotten by the world for centuries, and found again by a man in a hat.
An Inca emperor's mountain retreat, I'm guarded today by llamas and a peak shaped like a sleeping face.
The Inca citadel in the Andes of Peru.
fact: Machu Picchu was built in the 1400s, likely as an estate for the Inca emperor Pachacuti.

name: Iguazu Falls, Argentina and Brazil
clues: When a first lady saw me, she sighed 'poor Niagara'; I am 275 waterfalls that share one devil's throat.
I sit where two countries meet, and you can feel my spray from either side.
Giant waterfalls on the Argentina and Brazil border.
fact: Iguazu is made of about 275 separate waterfalls spread over nearly 3 km.

name: Milford Sound, New Zealand
clues: I'm called a sound but I'm really a fjord, carved by ice and drenched by some of the world's heaviest rains.
My cliffs rise straight from the water, and waterfalls appear on them after every storm.
A deep fjord in the far southwest of New Zealand's South Island.
fact: Milford Sound gets about 6.8 m of rain a year, making it one of the wettest places on Earth.

name: Golden Temple, Amritsar, India
clues: I'm a golden house in a pool of nectar, and my kitchen feeds a hundred thousand guests a day for free.
Anyone may eat at my table, no matter their faith, as long as they cover their head.
The holiest shrine of Sikhism, covered in gold.
fact: Anyone can eat at the Golden Temple's langar, whatever their religion.

name: Serengeti, Tanzania
clues: My name means endless plains, and every year two million hooves follow the rain in a great circle.
Lions rule my grass, and the greatest migration on land crosses me before heading north.
A famous savanna national park in Tanzania.
fact: The great migration includes about 1.5 million wildebeest plus hundreds of thousands of zebras.

name: Twelve Apostles, Australia
clues: They named us for the twelve, though we were never more than nine, and the sea keeps taking us one by one.
We're limestone stacks standing in the surf beside a famous coastal road.
Limestone stacks along the Great Ocean Road.
fact: The cliffs here retreat about 2 cm a year.

name: Great Pyramid of Giza, Egypt
clues: For almost four thousand years nothing humans built stood taller than me.
I'm the last of seven wonders still standing, and a king's tomb sits inside my stone.
The great pyramids just outside Cairo.
fact: The Great Pyramid was originally covered in polished white limestone that made it shine in the sun.

name: Pamukkale, Turkey
clues: I look like a frozen waterfall of snow, but I'm warm enough to bathe in.
My name means 'cotton castle', and a Roman city sits on my white terraces.
Pamukkale, in southwestern Turkey.
fact: Visitors to Pamukkale must walk the terraces barefoot to protect the soft travertine.

name: Uluru, Australia
clues: I'm a single stone that blushes red at sunset, and I'm older than the dinosaurs.
My owners asked visitors to stop climbing me, and in 2019 they finally did.
Uluru, also called Ayers Rock.
fact: Uluru is about 348 m high and 9.4 km around at its base.

name: Bran Castle, Romania
clues: A novelist gave me a vampire, though the real prince who inspired him barely visited.
I sit high on a rock in Transylvania, and my towers look exactly like a horror film poster.
A castle in the Carpathians near Brașov.
fact: Bram Stoker never visited Romania.

name: Stonehenge, England
clues: I'm a calendar made of giants, and on the longest day the sun rises right where I expect it.
Nobody knows exactly how my stones were dragged here, some of them from 200 km away.
Stonehenge, on Salisbury Plain.
fact: Stonehenge's biggest stones, the sarsens, weigh around 25 tonnes each.

name: Stone Town, Zanzibar, Tanzania
clues: My doors are carved and studded with spikes, built to keep out elephants that never came.
A rock star was born in my maze of alleys, on a spice island off East Africa.
The old town of a spice island off Tanzania.
fact: Zanzibar was famous for cloves and was once the world's largest producer.

name: Reine, Lofoten, Norway
clues: I'm a village painted red on a rock in the Arctic sea, and cod hang drying on my racks in spring.
My mountains rise straight from the water, and the midnight sun lights me all summer.
A fishing village in the Lofoten Islands.
fact: Lofoten is far north of the Arctic Circle but has a mild climate thanks to the Gulf Stream.

name: Pripyat and Chernobyl, Ukraine
clues: I'm a city that stopped in one afternoon in 1986, and the forest is slowly moving into my flats.
My Ferris wheel never had its opening day, and the reactor next to me is why.
The abandoned city next to the Chernobyl nuclear plant.
fact: The New Safe Confinement arch over Chernobyl's reactor is one of the largest movable structures ever built.

name: St Peter's Basilica, Vatican City
clues: I'm the biggest church in the smallest country, and a fisherman is said to be buried under me.
My dome was designed by a man who also painted a famous ceiling next door.
The great church of the Pope.
fact: Vatican City covers just 0.44 square kilometers.

name: Kīlauea, Hawaii, USA
clues: I'm a goddess's home, and I've been building new land for decades, one glowing river at a time.
My name means 'spewing', and I'm one of the most active volcanoes on Earth.
A volcano on Hawaii's Big Island.
fact: Kīlauea erupted almost continuously from 1983 to 2018.

name: Venice, Italy
clues: I have streets but no cars, and my buildings stand on millions of wooden legs.
I'm sinking slowly, and my rush hour happens on boats.
The Italian city of gondolas and canals.
fact: The wooden piles under Venice have lasted centuries because, without oxygen underwater, they slowly turned almost to stone.

name: Great Blue Hole, Belize
clues: I'm a perfect dark circle in a turquoise sea, an underwater cave whose roof fell in.
Divers drop into me to see stalactites that formed when I was dry land.
The Great Blue Hole, off the coast of Belize.
fact: The Great Blue Hole is about 300 m across and 125 m deep.

name: Acropolis, Athens, Greece
clues: I'm a rock crowned with marble temples to a goddess of wisdom, and her city took her name.
My most famous temple has no straight lines, every column is curved to look straight.
The rock above Athens, crowned by the Parthenon.
fact: The Parthenon was finished in 432 BC and dedicated to the goddess Athena.

name: Mont-Saint-Michel, France
clues: Twice a day I'm an island and twice a day I'm not, and an archangel tops my spire.
My tides race in 'as fast as a galloping horse', around a monastery on a rock.
A tidal island abbey off the coast of Normandy.
fact: The tides around Mont-Saint-Michel are among the strongest in Europe, up to 14 m.

name: Zhangjiajie, China
clues: My stone pillars float in mist, and they inspired the floating mountains of a famous blue film.
I'm a forest of sandstone towers, with a glass bridge strung between them.
A forest park of stone towers in Hunan.
fact: One pillar was renamed 'Avatar Hallelujah Mountain' in 2010.

name: Old Faithful, Yellowstone, USA
clues: I'm punctual, roughly every hour and a half I throw a fountain of boiling water into the sky.
I sit in the world's first national park, on top of a sleeping supervolcano.
The famous geyser in the world's first national park.
fact: Old Faithful erupts roughly every 60 to 110 minutes.

name: Terracotta Army, Xi'an, China
clues: Eight thousand soldiers guard me, and not one of them has ever moved or spoken.
A farmer digging a well found us in 1974, an emperor's army made of clay.
Clay warriors guarding China's first emperor.
fact: About 8,000 soldiers, 130 chariots and 670 horses are thought to be buried there.

name: Varanasi, India
clues: I'm one of the oldest living cities on Earth, and my stone steps lead down into a holy river.
Fires burn on my riverbank day and night, because dying here is said to free the soul.
One of the oldest living cities, on the Ganges.
fact: Varanasi has more than 80 ghats along the Ganges.

name: Sossusvlei, Namibia
clues: My dunes are red as rust and among the tallest anywhere, and dead trees stand in a white clay pan.
My name means 'dead-end marsh', a place where a river gives up in the sand.
Red sand dunes in the Namib Desert.
fact: The Namib is often called the oldest desert in the world, at around 55 million years.

name: Bagan, Myanmar
clues: Over two thousand temples spread across my plain, and the best way to see them is from a balloon.
Kings built me in a building spree a thousand years ago along the Irrawaddy.
An ancient temple city on the Irrawaddy River in Myanmar.
fact: Over 10,000 temples were built at Bagan between the 11th and 13th centuries.

name: Taj Mahal, India
clues: A grieving emperor built me for his wife, and I change color with the light of day.
My white marble is inlaid with gems, and my four towers lean slightly out on purpose.
The Taj Mahal in Agra.
fact: The four minarets of the Taj Mahal lean slightly outward so they would fall away from the tomb in an earthquake.

name: Statue of Liberty, New York, USA
clues: I'm a gift from one country to another, and my green skin was copper brown when I arrived.
I hold a torch and a tablet, and millions once saw me as their first view of a new home.
A torch-bearing gift from France in New York Harbor.
fact: The Statue of Liberty's index finger is about 2.4 m long.

name: Gorée Island, Senegal
clues: My 'door of no return' looks out to the Atlantic, and the world comes to remember what happened here.
I'm a small island with pastel houses off a capital city, now a place of memory.
A small island off Dakar, Senegal.
fact: Gorée became one of UNESCO's first World Heritage Sites in 1978.

name: Lake Natron, Tanzania
clues: My water is red, my mud is deadly, and yet flamingos raise their chicks on me.
Animals that die in me can turn as stiff as statues, thanks to my soda and salt.
A red soda lake in northern Tanzania.
fact: Lake Natron's red color comes from tiny salt-loving microorganisms.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro, Tanzania
clues: I'm a mountain that stands alone, wears snow at the equator, and you can walk all the way to my top.
I'm the roof of a continent, made of three volcanoes.
Africa's highest peak, in Tanzania.
fact: Kilimanjaro's summit, Uhuru Peak, is 5,895 m above sea level.

name: Hollywood Sign, Los Angeles, USA
clues: Nine letters on a hillside, and I started life as an advert for houses.
I lost four letters in 1949, and now I'm the most famous name in film.
White letters on a hillside above Los Angeles.
fact: The sign originally read HOLLYWOODLAND. The last four letters were removed in 1949.

name: Wadi Rum, Jordan
clues: They call me the Valley of the Moon, but film crews come to me to play Mars.
A famous British officer rode through my red sands and pink cliffs a century ago.
The Valley of the Moon desert in southern Jordan.
fact: Wadi Rum has stood in for Mars in films like The Martian.

name: Tristan da Cunha
clues: I'm the most remote place where people live: the nearest neighbours are 2,400 km of ocean away.
I'm a volcano with one village, and a ship visits just a few times a year.
A volcanic island in the middle of the South Atlantic.
fact: Tristan da Cunha has no airport. It takes about a week by boat from South Africa.

name: Chocolate Hills, Bohol, Philippines
clues: I'm more than a thousand hills that turn brown in the dry season, as if made of something sweet.
Legend says giants threw mud at each other here, and the hills are what's left.
Cone-shaped hills on Bohol island.
fact: There are at least 1,260 Chocolate Hills.

name: Lake Baikal, Russia
clues: I'm the deepest lake on Earth and hold a fifth of all the world's unfrozen fresh water.
I freeze so clear in winter that you can see the fish through my ice, and my seals live nowhere else.
Lake Baikal.
fact: Lake Baikal is about 25 million years old and more than 1,600 m deep.

name: Nazca Lines, Peru
clues: I drew a monkey, a hummingbird and a spider so big that only birds could see them.
My pictures are scratched in the desert, and they've barely changed in two thousand years.
Giant desert drawings in southern Peru.
fact: The lines have survived so long because the area gets almost no rain or wind.

name: Petra, Jordan
clues: A rose-red city half as old as time, my front door is a treasury carved straight into a cliff.
Caravans once paid my traders for water, and adventurers in films ride out of my canyon.
The ancient Nabataean city of Petra.
fact: Scientists estimate that around 85% of Petra is still buried and unexcavated.

name: Great Wall of China (Badaling)
clues: I'm a dragon of stone that crawls over mountains for thousands of kilometres.
Millions walk my oldest-looking section near a capital, and it's often busier than a city street.
The Great Wall of China, at Badaling near Beijing.
fact: All the sections of the Great Wall added together stretch about 21,000 km.

name: Mount Bromo, Indonesia
clues: I'm a smoking volcano rising from a sea of sand, and people ride horses to my rim at dawn.
Once a year, people throw vegetables and goats into my crater as offerings.
An active volcano in East Java.
fact: The Tenggerese people hold the Yadnya Kasada festival at Bromo every year.

name: Bora Bora, French Polynesia
clues: I'm a lagoon so blue it looks fake, and people sleep in huts standing over my water.
An extinct volcano sits in my middle, ringed by a reef and a few small islands.
An island in French Polynesia.
fact: Overwater bungalows were invented in French Polynesia in the 1960s.

name: Lake Hillier, Australia
clues: I'm a lake as pink as bubblegum, next to a sea that's blue.
Tiny algae give me my color, on an island off the south coast of a huge country.
A pink lake on an island off Western Australia.
fact: Lake Hillier's color comes from salt-loving algae and microbes.

name: Victoria Peak, Hong Kong
clues: I'm the highest seat in a city of skyscrapers, and a tram has climbed me since 1888.
From my top, the harbor lights look like a carpet of stars.
The highest hill on Hong Kong Island.
fact: Hong Kong has more skyscrapers than any other city in the world.

name: Rock of Gibraltar
clues: I'm a rock with a monkey colony, and legend says if they leave, the British will too.
I'm a pillar of Hercules, guarding the narrow gate between two seas.
A British limestone rock at the tip of Spain.
fact: About 300 Barbary macaques live on the Rock of Gibraltar.

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa, Italy
clues: I'm famous for a mistake: soft ground made me tilt before my builders even finished.
People take photos pretending to hold me up, in a white marble square called the Field of Miracles.
A tilted bell tower in Tuscany.
fact: The tower took about 200 years to build, partly because wars kept stopping the work.

name: Darvaza Gas Crater, Turkmenistan
clues: Geologists lit me in 1971 thinking I'd burn out in weeks, and I'm still burning.
Locals call me the door to hell, a fiery pit in the middle of a desert.
A burning crater in the Karakum Desert.
fact: The crater is about 70 m wide and has been burning for decades.

name: Edinburgh Castle, Scotland
clues: I sit on an extinct volcano, and every afternoon but Sunday I fire a gun to tell the time.
Crown jewels and the Stone of Destiny rest inside my walls above a royal mile.
The castle on the rock above Scotland's capital.
fact: The One O'Clock Gun has been fired since 1861 so ships could set their clocks.

name: Christ the Redeemer, Rio de Janeiro
clues: My arms are always open, I stand above a city of samba, and lightning hits me every year.
I'm made of soapstone tiles, on top of a mountain shaped like a hunchback.
The Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
fact: Christ the Redeemer was finished in 1931 and is about 30 m tall, not counting its pedestal.

name: Sagrada Família, Barcelona, Spain
clues: I've been under construction since 1882, and my architect said, 'My client is not in a hurry.'
My columns look like trees, and my towers are meant to reach the height of a hill but no higher.
Gaudí's giant basilica in Barcelona.
fact: Antoni Gaudí worked on the Sagrada Família for more than 40 years, until his death in 1926.

name: Panmunjom, Korean DMZ
clues: I'm a blue hut sliced in half by a border, and soldiers stare at each other across a concrete line.
Peace talks happen in my rooms, where the two halves of one peninsula meet.
The truce village on the border between the two Koreas.
fact: The Demilitarized Zone is about 4 km wide and 250 km long.

name: Mount Fuji, Japan
clues: I'm a nearly perfect cone, snow-capped and sacred, and on clear days a capital city can see me.
Climbers walk me at night to see the first sunrise from my rim.
A snow-capped volcano and the tallest peak in Japan.
fact: Mount Fuji is 3,776 m tall, and the official climbing season lasts only about two months each summer.

name: Malé, Maldives
clues: I'm a capital packed onto a tiny island, and my whole country sits barely higher than the waves.
From the air I look like a city floating on turquoise, among hundreds of coral atolls.
The capital of an island nation in the Indian Ocean.
fact: The Maldives is the flattest country in the world.

name: Brandenburg Gate, Berlin, Germany
clues: A chariot of four horses rides on top of me, and for decades a wall ran right past my door.
I was once a city gate, and now I'm a symbol of a country reunited.
The famous gate in the heart of Berlin.
fact: The Berlin Wall ran right beside the Brandenburg Gate from 1961 to 1989.

name: Wieliczka Salt Mine, Poland
clues: I'm a cathedral carved entirely from salt, with chandeliers made of crystals, deep underground.
Miners dug me for seven hundred years, and now visitors walk my tunnels.
An old salt mine near Kraków.
fact: Salt was mined at Wieliczka from the 13th century until 1996.

name: Angkor Wat, Cambodia
clues: I'm the largest religious building in the world, and I appear on a country's flag.
My towers look like lotus buds, and they shine in the reflecting pond at sunrise.
Angkor Wat temple in Cambodia.
fact: Angkor Wat faces west, which is unusual for a temple of its kind, and the sun rises right behind its towers at the equinox.

name: Dead Sea
clues: I'm a sea so salty you float like a cork, and I'm the lowest place on land.
Nothing swims in me, and I'm shrinking by about a metre a year.
A lake so salty it is called 'dead'.
fact: The Dead Sea's shore is about 430 m below sea level and the water level drops about 1 m a year.

name: Hampi, India
clues: I'm a lost capital of giant boulders, scattered as if a giant had been playing marbles.
Temples and ruins of a great kingdom lie among my rocks and banana fields.
The ruins of the Vijayanagara capital in Karnataka.
fact: Hampi's stone chariot at the Vittala Temple appears on India's 50-rupee note.

name: Kirkjufell, Iceland
clues: I'm a mountain shaped like an arrowhead, and a waterfall poses in front of me for every photograph.
A famous fantasy series filmed me, and I'm the most photographed peak on my island.
A cone-shaped mountain on Iceland's Snæfellsnes peninsula.
fact: Kirkjufell means 'church mountain'.

name: Badwater Basin, Death Valley, USA
clues: A surveyor's mule wouldn't drink from my pool, and I'm the lowest point in North America.
My salt floor cracks into hexagons, in a valley known for record heat.
A salt flat in Death Valley, California.
fact: Mount Whitney, the highest point in the lower 48 states, is less than 140 km from Badwater.

name: Tiger's Nest Monastery, Bhutan
clues: A guru is said to have flown me in on a tigress's back, and I cling to a cliff 900 metres up.
Monks live in my white buildings on the side of a gorge.
Paro Taktsang, a monastery in Bhutan.
fact: Bhutan measures its progress with Gross National Happiness.

name: Victoria Falls, Zambia and Zimbabwe
clues: My local name means 'the smoke that thunders', and my mist rises like a cloud for kilometres.
I'm the largest sheet of falling water in the world, between two countries.
Victoria Falls on the Zambezi River.
fact: At full flood, more than 500 million liters of water per minute pour over Victoria Falls.

name: Lalibela, Ethiopia
clues: My churches are carved down into the rock, not built up, as if someone sculpted the ground itself.
A king wanted to build a new Jerusalem, and eleven churches came out of the stone.
Rock-hewn churches in the Ethiopian highlands.
fact: Lalibela's 11 churches were carved around the 12th and 13th centuries and are still used for worship.

name: Svalbard (Longyearbyen), Norway
clues: I'm a town where it's against the rules to die, and polar bears may be your neighbours.
A seed vault built in my mountain keeps the world's crops safe.
Longyearbyen, the main town of Svalbard.
fact: The Global Seed Vault holds more than a million seed samples from almost every country.

name: Times Square, New York City
clues: My new year starts with a falling ball, and my glowing screens never let the night get dark.
I'm known as the crossroads of the world, in a city that never sleeps.
Times Square, Manhattan.
fact: The New Year's Eve ball drop in Times Square started in 1907.

name: Shibuya Crossing, Tokyo, Japan
clues: When my lights turn green, thousands walk at once in every direction, even diagonally.
A loyal dog's statue waits for its owner at my station.
The world's busiest pedestrian crossing, in Tokyo.
fact: The dog Hachikō waited at Shibuya Station for his owner every day for nearly ten years.

name: Preikestolen, Norway
clues: I'm a flat-topped cliff like a pulpit, hanging over a fjord, and there's no railing.
A two-hour hike leads to my edge, 600 metres above the water.
A cliff above the Lysefjord in Norway.
fact: About 300,000 people hike to Preikestolen each year.

name: Alhambra, Granada, Spain
clues: My name means 'the red one', and inside I'm covered in poems carved into the walls.
The last kingdom of its kind in my country surrendered here in 1492.
A Moorish palace above Granada.
fact: The Alhambra was the last stronghold of Muslim rule in Spain, until 1492.

name: Torres del Paine, Chile
clues: My towers are granite horns, and my winds can knock a hiker over.
I'm a national park at the end of the Andes, with blue lakes and guanacos.
A national park in Chilean Patagonia.
fact: 'Paine' is thought to mean 'blue' in the local Tehuelche language.

name: Registan, Samarkand, Uzbekistan
clues: Three schools face each other across my square, covered in blue tiles that glitter in the sun.
I stood at the heart of a city on the Silk Road, once Tamerlane's capital.
The famous square of Samarkand.
fact: Registan means 'sandy place' in Persian.

name: Komodo Island, Indonesia
clues: I'm home to the world's largest living lizards, dragons that can smell blood from kilometres away.
I'm an island in a national park, with a beach that looks pink.
An island in the Lesser Sunda chain, home of dragons.
fact: Komodo dragons can grow to 3 m long.

name: Tikal, Guatemala
clues: My temples poke above the jungle canopy, and a famous space film used me as a rebel base.
Howler monkeys shout from my trees, and I was once a great Maya city.
A great Maya city in the jungle of northern Guatemala.
fact: Tikal appeared as the Rebel base on Yavin 4 in the first Star Wars film in 1977.

name: Ilulissat Icefjord, Greenland
clues: I'm a fjord that births icebergs, and one of my children may have sunk a famous ship.
My glacier is among the fastest in the world, near a town on a giant island.
An icefjord on Greenland's west coast.
fact: Sermeq Kujalleq glacier produces about 10% of Greenland's icebergs.

name: Colosseum, Rome, Italy
clues: I once held fifty thousand people who came to watch fights, and my floor could be flooded for boat battles.
I'm half broken, but I'm still the biggest amphitheatre ever built.
The great amphitheater of the Roman emperors.
fact: Much of the Colosseum's missing stone was taken to build other buildings in Rome, including St Peter's.

name: Ushuaia, Argentina
clues: I call myself the end of the world, and ships leave me for the last continent.
I'm the southernmost city of my kind, on the Beagle Channel.
The southernmost city on the island of Tierra del Fuego.
fact: Ushuaia was founded around a prison, which is now a museum.

name: Borobudur, Indonesia
clues: Seen from above, I'm a giant flower, and 504 Buddhas sit on my terraces.
I was hidden under volcanic ash and jungle for centuries, on the island of Java.
The largest Buddhist temple in the world, on the island of Java.
fact: Borobudur was built in the 9th century from about two million stone blocks.

name: Havana, Cuba
clues: My streets are full of old American cars, and my music never stops.
My seafront wall is the living room of my city, where waves crash at sunset.
The capital of Cuba.
fact: Old Havana and its fortifications became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982.

name: Table Mountain, Cape Town, South Africa
clues: I'm a mountain with a flat top, and a white cloud called the tablecloth sometimes covers me.
A cable car turns as it climbs me, above a city at the tip of a continent.
The flat-topped mountain above Cape Town.
fact: The constellation Mensa, 'the table', was named after Table Mountain in the 1750s.

name: Angel Falls, Venezuela
clues: I'm the tallest waterfall in the world, and a pilot who crashed on my mountain gave me his name.
My water falls almost a kilometre from a flat-topped mountain in the jungle.
The world's tallest waterfall, in Venezuela.
fact: Angel Falls drops 979 m, with an unbroken fall of 807 m.

name: Dubrovnik, Croatia
clues: Thick walls wrap my red roofs, and a fantasy series used me as its capital.
I'm called the Pearl of the Adriatic, a walled city on the sea.
A walled old town on the Adriatic coast.
fact: Dubrovnik's walls are nearly 2 km around and up to 25 m high.

name: Thingvellir, Iceland
clues: Two continents' plates pull apart through my valley, and the world's oldest parliament met here.
You can dive between two continents in my clear water.
Thingvellir (Þingvellir), Iceland.
fact: The rift valley at Thingvellir widens by about 2 cm every year.

name: Cartagena, Colombia
clues: My walls once kept out pirates, and my balconies drip with flowers.
I'm a colorful port on the Caribbean coast of South America.
A walled Caribbean port city in Colombia.
fact: Cartagena's city walls stretch about 11 km.

name: Lake Titicaca, Peru and Bolivia
clues: I'm the highest lake big ships can sail, and some people here live on islands made of reeds.
Legend says the sun was born from my water, on the border of two countries.
The highest navigable lake in the world, between Peru and Bolivia.
fact: Lake Titicaca sits about 3,812 m above sea level.

name: Chefchaouen, Morocco
clues: I'm a mountain town painted every shade of blue, as if the sky had fallen into my streets.
I'm hidden in the Rif mountains, and my cats nap on blue steps.
The blue city of northern Morocco.
fact: Chefchaouen was founded in 1471 as a small fortress.

name: Great Barrier Reef, Australia
clues: I'm the largest living structure on Earth, visible from space, built by tiny animals.
Clownfish and turtles live in my coral, along the coast of a huge island.
The giant coral reef off Queensland.
fact: The Great Barrier Reef is made of about 2,900 individual reefs.

name: Pompeii, Italy
clues: I'm a city frozen in one moment, buried by a mountain's ash in a single day.
Volcanic ash kept my streets, bread and graffiti for almost two thousand years.
A Roman town at the foot of Mount Vesuvius.
fact: Pompeii was rediscovered in the 1700s, about 1,600 years after it was buried.

name: Moraine Lake, Canada
clues: My water is so blue it was printed on a banknote, below ten jagged peaks.
A glacier's fine dust gives me my color in the Rocky Mountains.
A glacier lake below ten peaks in Banff National Park.
fact: Moraine Lake is usually frozen until June.

name: Las Vegas Strip, USA
clues: My nights are brighter than my days, and a pyramid shines a beam into space.
I'm a desert boulevard of casinos and copies of the world's famous sights.
The neon street of casinos in Nevada.
fact: The beam of light from the top of the Luxor pyramid is among the strongest in the world.

name: St Basil's Cathedral, Moscow, Russia
clues: I wear nine onion hats, each striped like a candy, and legend says my builder was blinded so I'd never be copied.
I stand at the edge of a red square that wasn't named for its color, beside a fortress with a ruby star.
The colorful cathedral on Red Square.
fact: St Basil's was built in the 1550s to celebrate a military victory by Ivan the Terrible.

name: Forbidden City, Beijing, China
clues: Nine thousand rooms are said to hide in me, yet for five hundred years commoners could not step inside.
Emperors ruled from my yellow roofs, and my front gate wears a giant portrait over a vast square.
The imperial palace in the heart of Beijing.
fact: The Forbidden City was home to 24 emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties.

name: Arctic Circle, Rovaniemi, Finland
clues: Cross my painted line and the sun may refuse to set in summer or rise in winter, and a bearded man in red keeps an office here.
Reindeer and letters from children all find their way to me, in Lapland.
Santa Claus Village on the Arctic Circle in Finland.
fact: Santa's main post office in Rovaniemi gets letters from about 200 countries.

name: Mount Everest
clues: I grow a few millimeters every year, though no one can climb higher than me without wings.
Locals call me Mother of the World, and my summit sits on a border between two countries in the Himalaya.
The highest point on Earth above sea level.
fact: The summit of Everest is made of marine limestone. It was once the floor of an ancient sea.

name: Burj Khalifa, Dubai, UAE
clues: My shadow can be seen from far out in the desert, and you can watch the sunset twice in one day by riding my elevator.
A needle of glass taller than any other, I rise above a city of gold souks and artificial islands.
The tallest building in the world, in Dubai.
fact: The Burj Khalifa is 828 m tall and opened in 2010.

name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial, Japan
clues: My dome is only a skeleton, and I was kept that way on purpose, so the world would never forget one August morning.
Paper cranes are folded for a girl who lived nearby, and the city around me rose again from ashes.
The A-Bomb Dome in Hiroshima.
fact: The dome was one of the few buildings left standing near the hypocenter on 6 August 1945.

name: Amsterdam, Netherlands
clues: I have more bicycles than people and more bridges than Venice, and my houses lean like tired friends.
My canals ring the old town in half-circles, and a diary written in a hidden annex is read here by millions.
The Dutch capital of canals.
fact: Amsterdam's 17th-century canal ring is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Big Ben, London, England
clues: People call me by the name of my bell, not my real name, and my four faces keep a nation on time.
I chime beside a river and a Parliament, and I was renamed for a queen's jubilee.
The clock tower at the Houses of Parliament in London.
fact: The tower was renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012 for Queen Elizabeth II's Diamond Jubilee.

name: Avenue of the Baobabs, Madagascar
clues: We are upside-down trees, roots in the sky, lining a dusty road at sunset.
We may be eight hundred years old, on an island that split from Africa long ago, and lemurs live nowhere else but here.
A road of giant baobab trees near Morondava.
fact: Six of the world's eight baobab species grow only in Madagascar.

name: Socotra, Yemen
clues: My trees look like umbrellas turned inside out, and they bleed red sap called dragon's blood.
A third of my plants grow nowhere else on Earth, on an island far off the Horn of Africa.
Socotra island, part of Yemen.
fact: The red resin of Socotra's dragon's blood tree has been traded since ancient times as dye and medicine.

name: Alcatraz, San Francisco, USA
clues: I was called the Rock, and the cold currents around me were my real guards.
Al Capone slept here, and three men may or may not have escaped me on a raft made of raincoats.
The prison island in San Francisco Bay.
fact: Alcatraz was a federal prison from 1934 to 1963. Al Capone was one of its inmates.

name: Niagara Falls, Canada and USA
clues: I am three curtains of water that never close, and daredevils have tumbled over me in barrels.
I sit between two great lakes and two countries, and honeymooners come in boats called Maid of the Mist.
Three waterfalls on the border between Ontario and New York.
fact: Annie Edson Taylor was the first person to survive going over Niagara Falls in a barrel.

name: Grand Canyon, Arizona, USA
clues: Two billion years of Earth's diary are written in my red walls, and a river carved every page.
I'm a mile deep in places, and some visitors walk out over me on a glass horseshoe.
A mile-deep canyon cut by the Colorado River in Arizona.
fact: The Grand Canyon is about 446 km long and up to 29 km wide.

name: Meeting of the Waters, Manaus, Brazil
clues: Coffee and milk flow side by side here for miles, refusing to mix.
A black river and a sandy one meet near a city with an opera house built during the rubber boom.
Where the Rio Negro meets the Amazon, in Brazil.
fact: The two rivers differ in temperature, speed and density, which keeps them apart.

name: Teotihuacan, Mexico
clues: I am the city of the gods, so old that even the Aztecs found me in ruins and gave me my name.
My Avenue of the Dead leads past a pyramid of the Sun to a pyramid of the Moon.
The Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, near Mexico City.
fact: At its peak around 500 AD, Teotihuacan may have had more than 100,000 people.

name: Galapagos Islands, Ecuador
clues: My tortoises are older than your grandparents, and my finches helped a young naturalist change science.
I'm a volcanic archipelago on the equator, where iguanas swim and blue-footed boobies dance.
The Galapagos Islands, part of Ecuador.
fact: Galapagos giant tortoises can live for more than 100 years.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle, Germany
clues: A dreamer king built me for himself and died before I was finished, and a famous mouse borrowed my look.
My white towers rise on a crag above a gorge, near the border of Austria, in Bavaria.
A fairy-tale castle in the Bavarian Alps.
fact: King Ludwig II of Bavaria died in 1886, before Neuschwanstein was finished.

name: Atomium, Brussels, Belgium
clues: I am a tiny piece of iron, blown up 165 billion times, so you can walk inside my atoms.
Built for a World's Fair in 1958, my nine shiny balls sit in the capital of Europe's institutions.
Nine giant silver balls in Brussels.
fact: The Atomium is 102 m tall, and you can ride an escalator between its spheres.

name: Salar de Uyuni, Bolivia
clues: After the rain I become the world's biggest mirror, and you can't tell where the ground ends and the sky begins.
I'm a white desert of salt high in the Andes, with a hotel built of salt blocks and a train graveyard nearby.
The biggest salt flat in the world, high in the Andes of Bolivia.
fact: Salar de Uyuni covers more than 10,000 square kilometers and varies in height by less than a meter.

name: McMurdo Station, Antarctica
clues: I'm the biggest town on the coldest continent, and in summer more than a thousand people live here.
I sit on an island near a smoking volcano, beside a hut left by Captain Scott.
The main US research base in Antarctica.
fact: McMurdo can house about 1,000 people in the summer.

name: San Pedro de Atacama, Chile
clues: Some of my neighbors have never seen rain, so NASA tests Mars rovers nearby.
I'm an adobe oasis town near geysers, salt flats and a Valley of the Moon, in the driest desert on Earth.
An oasis town in the driest non-polar desert on Earth.
fact: The Atacama is so dry and clear that it hosts some of the world's largest telescopes.

name: Hallstatt, Austria
clues: My village is so pretty it was copied, house for house, on the other side of the world.
Squeezed between a lake and the mountains, I have a bone house and one of the oldest salt mines on Earth.
A lakeside village in the Austrian Alps.
fact: Hallstatt's bone house holds hundreds of painted skulls, because the tiny graveyard ran out of space.

name: Ha Long Bay, Vietnam
clues: Legend says a dragon came down to fight invaders and spat out jewels that became my islands.
Nearly two thousand limestone islands rise from my green water, where junk boats drift in the Gulf of Tonkin.
A bay of green islands in northern Vietnam.
fact: Ha Long means 'descending dragon' in Vietnamese.

name: Belém Tower, Lisbon, Portugal
clues: I was a sailor's last sight of home, and I wear a stone rope and a rhinoceros on my walls.
I guard the river where explorers set off for India and Brazil, in the city of trams and custard tarts.
A riverside fortress at the mouth of the Tagus in Lisbon.
fact: The rhino carving is thought to show the rhinoceros sent to Lisbon from India in 1515.

name: Hagia Sophia, Istanbul, Türkiye
clues: I've been a church, a mosque, a museum and a mosque again, and my dome seems to float on a ring of light.
For nearly a thousand years I was the biggest cathedral on Earth, on the strait between two continents.
The great domed building of old Constantinople.
fact: Hagia Sophia's main dome rises about 55 m above the floor.

name: Persepolis, Iran
clues: A conqueror burned me after a party, but my stone gate of winged bulls still says All Nations.
Kings of kings received gifts from every land on my staircases, near the city of Shiraz.
The ceremonial capital of the ancient Persian Empire.
fact: Persepolis was founded by Darius the Great around 518 BC.

name: Oia, Santorini, Greece
clues: My houses are sugar cubes and my domes are pieces of sky, perched on the rim of a sunken volcano.
Crowds clap here every evening for the sunset, on a crescent island in the Cyclades.
White houses and blue domes on a Greek island in the Aegean.
fact: The Minoan eruption of Santorini was one of the largest volcanic eruptions in human history.

name: Sydney Opera House, Australia
clues: I look like a ship full of sails, or a pile of seashells, and my roof wears more than a million tiles.
A Danish architect designed me, and my curved shells were cut like segments of an orange, on a famous harbor.
White sails on a harbour, near a famous bridge nicknamed the Coathanger.
fact: Danish architect Jørn Utzon resigned in 1966 and never returned to see the finished building.

name: Göreme, Cappadocia, Türkiye
clues: My chimneys are made of stone and fairies, and my churches were carved inside them.
At dawn the sky fills with hot-air balloons above my valleys, and whole cities hide underground nearby.
The land of fairy chimneys in central Türkiye.
fact: Derinkuyu, an underground city nearby, goes down about 85 m and could shelter thousands.

name: Hobbiton, Matamata, New Zealand
clues: My doors are round and my residents are short, but no one has ever really lived here.
I'm a village of green hillside holes on a sheep farm, with a party tree and a pub called the Green Dragon.
The hobbit village film set on New Zealand's North Island.
fact: Hobbiton was rebuilt in permanent materials for The Hobbit films and is now a tourist attraction.

name: Pyramids of Meroë, Sudan
clues: My pyramids are steep and slim, and there are more of us than in Egypt, yet hardly anyone visits.
I was the royal city of black pharaohs and warrior queens, along the Nile north of Khartoum.
The royal pyramids of ancient Kush, in Sudan.
fact: In the 1830s an Italian treasure hunter blew the tops off dozens of Meroë's pyramids looking for gold.

name: Petronas Towers, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
clues: We are twins holding hands in the sky, linked by a bridge on our 41st and 42nd floors.
Our steel shines like a temple's star pattern in a city whose name means muddy confluence.
Malaysia's famous twin skyscrapers.
fact: The Petronas Towers were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004.

name: Timbuktu, Mali
clues: People say I'm the end of the world, and many think I'm a made-up place.
Camel caravans brought salt and gold here, and my mosques of mud keep scholars' manuscripts, near the Niger.
A legendary desert city in Mali whose name starts with 'Tim'.
fact: Timbuktu's Djinguereber Mosque was built around 1327 and is still made of mud brick.

name: Monaco
clues: I'm smaller than a big city park, but I have a prince, a palace and a casino.
Once a year race cars scream through my streets and tunnel, on the Riviera.
A tiny principality on the French Riviera.
fact: Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world after Vatican City.

name: Fushimi Inari Shrine, Kyoto, Japan
clues: Ten thousand orange gates make a tunnel up my mountain, and stone foxes keep watch.
My shrine honors the god of rice, in Japan's old imperial capital.
Fushimi Inari shrine in Kyoto.
fact: The paths of torii gates at Fushimi Inari wind about 4 km up Mount Inari.

name: Jemaa el-Fnaa, Marrakech, Morocco
clues: By day I hold snake charmers and juice stalls, and by night I turn into a giant open-air kitchen.
My square lies below a tall minaret in a pink-walled city at the foot of the Atlas.
The great square of Morocco's Red City.
fact: The square was one of the first places on UNESCO's list of Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity in 2001.

name: Panama Canal, Panama
clues: Ships climb a watery staircase to cross me, and I made sailing around South America unnecessary.
I cut through a narrow country joining two continents, linking the Atlantic and Pacific.
The canal across a narrow Central American country.
fact: Each ship passing through the Panama Canal uses about 200 million liters of fresh water from Gatun Lake.

name: The South Pole
clues: Every direction from me points north, and you could walk around the world in a few seconds.
Amundsen beat Scott here in 1911, on top of three kilometers of ice.
The southern end of Earth's axis.
fact: The ice at the South Pole moves about 10 m a year, so the marker for the exact pole is moved every January.

name: Half Dome, Yosemite, USA
clues: Half of me is missing, or so it seems, and climbers pull themselves up my back on steel cables.
My sheer granite face looks down on a valley of giant sequoias and waterfalls in the Sierra Nevada.
A granite dome in Yosemite National Park, California.
fact: Half Dome rises about 1,444 m above the floor of Yosemite Valley.

name: Lake Bled, Slovenia
clues: Ring the bell on my only island and your wish may come true, if you climb 99 steps first.
My emerald lake has a castle on a cliff and famous cream cake, in the Julian Alps.
An alpine lake with a church on an island, in Slovenia.
fact: Bled's island is the only natural island in Slovenia.

name: Sigiriya, Sri Lanka
clues: A king built his palace on my head and entered through a lion's paws.
My walls once held painted maidens, and my rock rises 200 meters out of the jungle on a tropical island.
The Lion Rock fortress in Sri Lanka.
fact: Sigiriya was built by King Kashyapa in the 5th century.

name: Marina Bay Sands, Singapore
clues: Three towers carry a ship on their shoulders, and swimmers float in a pool at the edge of the sky.
I look over a garden of supertrees in a tiny city-state at the tip of the Malay Peninsula.
A famous hotel on the waterfront of a city-state.
fact: Singapore is one of only three surviving city-states.

name: Icehotel, Jukkasjärvi, Sweden
clues: I melt every spring and am rebuilt every winter, and even my beds and glasses are frozen.
I'm made from a river's ice, 200 km north of the Arctic Circle, where the northern lights dance.
A hotel made of ice in Swedish Lapland.
fact: The first Icehotel was built in 1989-90 on the Torne River.

name: Maya Bay, Thailand
clues: A movie made me so famous that I had to close for years to heal.
I'm a cove walled in by limestone cliffs, on an island in the Andaman Sea.
A cove on Ko Phi Phi Le in the Andaman Sea.
fact: Maya Bay was closed from 2018 to 2022 to let its coral and sharks recover.

name: Mount Rushmore, USA
clues: Our faces are 18 meters tall, and we never blink.
Four presidents are carved into my granite in the Black Hills.
Four presidents carved into a mountain in South Dakota.
fact: Carving Mount Rushmore took 14 years, from 1927 to 1941, mostly with dynamite.

name: Point Nemo, South Pacific
clues: My closest neighbors are often astronauts, and old spacecraft come here to die.
I'm the spot in the ocean farthest from any land, named after a fictional submarine captain.
The 'oceanic pole of inaccessibility', named after Jules Verne's submarine captain.
fact: The nearest land to Point Nemo is about 2,700 km away.

name: The Bund, Shanghai, China
clues: My grand old banks face a forest of futuristic towers across the river.
I'm a waterfront promenade of colonial-era buildings, in China's biggest city.
Shanghai's famous waterfront.
fact: The Shanghai Tower across the river is the tallest building in China.

name: Potala Palace, Lhasa, Tibet
clues: My thousand rooms climb a red hill, painted white for living and red for praying.
I was the winter home of the Dalai Lamas, on the roof of the world.
A red-and-white palace in Lhasa.
fact: The Potala Palace is 13 stories tall and was built in the 1600s on an older site.

name: Abu Simbel, Egypt
clues: Twice a year the sun reaches deep inside me and lights the faces of the gods.
My four giant kings were cut apart and moved uphill to escape a rising lake on the Nile.
Giant statues of Ramesses II near the Sudan border.
fact: Moving Abu Simbel took four years and a global campaign led by UNESCO.

name: Eiffel Tower, Paris, France
clues: I was meant to stand for only twenty years and grow about 15 cm taller in summer heat.
Built for a World's Fair in 1889, I'm the iron lady of the City of Light.
The iron lady on the Champ de Mars.
fact: The Eiffel Tower grows about 15 cm taller in summer as the iron expands in the heat.
